extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (patent owners and third-party requesters) handling ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance for conducting and responding to ex parte reexamination of U.S. patents, including when reexamination may be ordered, what issues may be considered, and requirements for correcting priority/benefit and inventorship during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on amended/new claims enlarging scope (35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: “No proposed amended or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim of the patent will be permitted in a reexamination proceeding....” A claim presented in a reexamination “enlarges the scope” where the claim is broader than each and every claim of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim is broader if it contains within its scope any conceivable product or process which would not have infringed the original patent. A claim is broadened if it is broader in any one respect, even though it may be narrower in other respects. Examiner Note: The claim limitations which are considered to broaden the scope should be identified and explained in bracket 2. See MPEP § 2258.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of claims subject to prior Office or court decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Where some patent claims in a patent being reexamined have been the subject of a prior Office or court decision, those circumstances must be addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent claims held invalid by a court should be identified. See MPEP § 2242. For handling a claim under reexamination which is dependent on a claim not subject to reexamination, see MPEP § 2260.01. All added claims will be examined. See MPEP §§ 2242, 2282–2286 for related procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation to 'live' claims and requester’s obligation (35 U.S.C. 302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reexamination is generally limited to review of the 'live' claims (existing claims not held invalid by a final decision) for which reexamination has been requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to every claim for which reexamination is requested (35 U.S.C. 302; 37 CFR 1.510(b)). If requester fails to apply the art to certain claims, requester is not statutorily entitled to reexamination of such claims. The Office may, in its sole discretion, reexamine claims for which reexamination was not requested (35 U.S.C. 303(a)), or initiate reexamination on its own initiative of non-requested claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to state non-patent/non-publication grounds from prior decisions (37 CFR 1.552(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 where grounds are set forth in a prior Office or federal court decision that are not based on patents or printed publications, the examiner’s Office action should clearly state that the claims have not been examined as to those non-patent/non-publication grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.552(c) and In re Knight, 217 USPQ 294 (Comm’r Pat. 1982). The Office action should explicitly note which grounds were not examined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction practice not permitted in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction requirements cannot be made in a reexamination proceeding because no statutory basis exists for restriction in a reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addition of claims to a 'separate and distinct' invention would be considered an enlargement of scope. See Ex parte Wikdahl, 10 USPQ2d 1546 (Bd. Pat. App. & Inter. 1989) and MPEP § 1412.03.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary amendments permitted to correct necessary patentability incidents
rubrics_metrics.description: Matters ancillary to reexamination that are necessary and incident to patentability will be considered; amendments may be made to correct e.g., inadvertent failure to claim foreign priority or continuing status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments to the specification may be allowed when necessary to overcome a reference applied against a claim, such as correcting priority or continuity information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination (37 CFR 1.324)
rubrics_metrics.description: Correction of inventorship may be made during reexamination via petition under 37 CFR 1.324.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.324 is granted, a Certificate of Correction will not be separately issued because the change-of-inventorship information is merged into the reexamination certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of affidavits in reexamination (37 CFR 1.131, 1.132)
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits under 37 CFR 1.131(a) and 1.132 may be utilized in a reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131(a) may not be used to 'swear behind' a reference patent if the reference patent is claiming the 'same invention' as the patent undergoing reexamination. In that situation, the patent owner may seek relief via an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131(c) (see MPEP § 718) or in an interference/derivation or via reissue if appropriate (see MPEP § 1449.02).

rubrics_metrics.name: Issues not within scope of ex parte reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain issues (e.g., public use/on sale, conduct issues, abandonment under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c), etc.) raised in a reexamination ordered under 35 U.S.C. 304 are not within the scope of that ex parte reexamination and will not be considered in the proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ¶ 22.03 form paragraph can be used to identify issues not within the scope. Such issues may be noted if raised by the patent owner or third-party requester, but the examiner should not independently raise them. If independently discovered by the examiner but not raised by the parties, the existence of such questions will not be noted by the examiner in an Office action (37 CFR 1.552(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to check prior file history for previously cited/considered art before making rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Before making a rejection based on art in reexamination, the examiner should check the patent's file history to determine if the art was previously cited/considered in earlier concluded Office examination(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For expediency this art is termed 'old art' (per In re Hiniker). If a rejection will be based on a combination of 'old art' and newly cited art, the rejection is proper (In re Hiniker). If old art alone is the basis, see separate criteria for reexamination ordered on/after Nov 2, 2002 and prior to that date.

rubrics_metrics.name: SNQ determinations for reexaminations ordered on or after November 2, 2002 (old art may suffice)
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered on or after Nov 2, 2002, reliance solely on old art does not necessarily preclude the existence of a substantial new question of patentability (SNQ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determinations are fact-specific and case-by-case; SNQ may be based solely on old art if the old art is presented/viewed in a new light or in view of material new argument/interpretation. When an Office action first sets forth an SNQ based solely on old art, include form paragraph 22.01.01 and explain specifics (identify old art in bracket 2 and explain why in bracket 3). See Pub. L. 107-273, Section 13105 and In re Chicago Rawhide Mfg. Co., 223 USPQ 351.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portola Packaging constraints for reexaminations ordered prior to November 2, 2002
rubrics_metrics.description: For reexaminations ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002, 'old art' generally cannot be used as the sole basis for a rejection, subject to exceptions outlined from In re Portola Packaging Inc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prior art was previously relied upon to reject a claim in a concluded prior related Office proceeding, the Office will not conduct reexamination based only on such prior art. If prior art was cited but its relevance to patentability was not discussed on the record of a prior related proceeding, reexamination may proceed based on that art. Records must show discussion; mere checkmarks or 'cited as background' do not preclude reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures to determine compliance with Portola Packaging (steps a–e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel must follow a procedural checklist when deciding whether prosecution of an ongoing reexamination ordered prior to Nov 2, 2002 must be terminated to comply with Portola Packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: (a) Ascertain order date; (b) determine for prior related proceedings what prior art was (i) relied upon to reject any claim or (ii) cited and discussed; (c) base rejections at least in part on prior art that in prior proceedings was neither relied upon nor cited+discussed; (d) withdraw rejections based only on prior art previously relied upon or cited+discussed; (e) terminate prosecution where only remaining rejections are entirely based on such prior art. Director may search for new art under 35 U.S.C. 303 prior to termination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling unusual fact patterns and when to involve TC/CRU Director
rubrics_metrics.description: Cases with unusual fact patterns relating to previous reliance or discussion of prior art should be brought to the attention of the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) or Technology Center (TC) Director for determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: (a) textbook was cited but only select information was discussed—indicate which portion was previously considered per 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2)(ii); (b) examiner previously misappreciated whether a reference qualified as prior art—new explanation may overcome that; (c) foreign language references previously cited but not fully/accurately translated—complete translation may support reexamination; (d) cumulative/repetitive references that substantially reiterate a previously applied reference may be treated as repetitive (rare). These examples are illustrative, not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notices and wording when terminating prosecution or withdrawing rejections under Portola Packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific language must be used in notices when prosecution is terminated or when rejections are withdrawn to comply with In re Portola Packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution is terminated under Portola Packaging, the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate should state: 'The prosecution of this reexamination is terminated based on In re Portola Packaging, Inc., 110 F.3d 786, 42 USPQ2d 1295 (Fed. Cir. 1997). No patentability determination has been made in this reexamination proceeding.' If a rejection is withdrawn, the Office action should state similar language noting withdrawal and that no patentability determination has been made in view of such prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming foreign priority during reexamination (general entitlement and perfection)
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may correct failure to adequately claim foreign priority in a patent being reexamined; perfection may require submission of a certified copy and possibly a petition depending on circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a priority claim was made before the patent was granted, submission of the certified copy in the reexamination proceeding may be sufficient to perfect priority. If a petition to accept a delayed certified copy under 37 CFR 1.55(f) or (g) is required, that petition (with fee and attachments) must be filed in the file of the application that matured into the patent, and a separate letter filed in the reexamination notifying the Office that the petition is being concurrently filed. Decisions on such petitions in the application file will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP § 215.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements when submitting a new foreign priority claim (items for on/after vs before Sept 16, 2012)
rubrics_metrics.description: When claiming foreign priority for the first time during reexamination, specific items must be filed in the application file that matured into the patent and a notifying letter placed in the reexamination file. Requirements differ by the filing date of the underlying application (on/after vs before Sept 16, 2012).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For applications filed on/after Sept 16, 2012, required items in the application file include: (a) grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.55(e); (b) application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76(b)(6)) identifying the foreign application; (c) certified copy of the foreign application (unless exception applies); (d) petition fee (37 CFR 1.17(m)); (e) statement that the entire delay was unintentional; and in the reexamination file (f) a separate letter notifying the Office that items (a)-(e) were or are being concurrently filed. For applications filed before Sept 16, 2012, similar requirements apply but alternatives for identifying the foreign application (ADS or oath/declaration) are permitted per 37 CFR 1.55(n). See MPEP § 214.02 for further guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoring right of foreign priority where filing of subsequent application was delayed (37 CFR 1.55(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may restore foreign priority rights where filing of the subsequent application was delayed by filing a grantable petition under 37 CFR 1.55(c) in the appropriate application file (not the reexamination file).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A letter must be filed in the reexamination proceeding as a separate paper notifying the Office that the petition and attachments were or are being concurrently filed in the application specified in 37 CFR 1.55(c). Decisions on the petition in that application file will be placed in the reexamination file; if granted, the application data sheet used to satisfy 37 CFR 1.55(c) requirements will be placed in the reexamination file. See MPEP § 213.03, subsection III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming domestic benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 during reexamination (petition under 37 CFR 1.78(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner may correct failure to adequately claim domestic benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 by filing a grantable petition for an unintentionally delayed benefit claim under 37 CFR 1.78(e) in the file of the application that matured into the patent, with a notifying letter placed in the reexamination file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition and required attachments (except certain specification amendments for pre-Sept 16, 2012 nonprovisional applications) must be filed in the application file which matured into the patent. The procedures and required items vary depending on whether the application that matured into the patent was filed on/after or before Sept 16, 2012; a letter must notify the reexamination file that the petition and attachments are being concurrently filed. See subsections II.A.1 and II.A.2 in MPEP § 2258.02 for itemized requirements.
